papers.title: Probiotics and diarrhoea morbidity among infants in Tanzania: secondary analysis of a randomised clinical trial.
papers.abstract: Diarrhoea causes annually more than 444 000 deaths in children globally, the majority in infants in low-income countries. The gut microbiota is a key determinant in resilience against enteric infections. We evaluated the effects of Bifidobacterium-based probiotic supplementation on diarrhoea morbidity among infants in Tanzania and explored associations between the gut microbiota composition at 6 weeks of age and later diarrhoeal risk.
papers.summary: This secondary analysis of a randomized clinical trial in Tanzania examined whether Bifidobacterium-based probiotic supplementation reduces diarrhoea morbidity in infants, and whether gut microbiota composition at 6 weeks of age predicts later diarrhoeal risk. The study links early-life microbiome features to enteric infection outcomes in a low-income setting where diarrhoea mortality is high.

papers.title: CAnDi: a global catalogue of anaerobic digestion microbiomes.
papers.abstract: Methanogenic environments harbour complex prokaryotic consortia that drive the anaerobic conversion of organic matter into methane and carbon dioxide. Beyond being key to the global carbon cycle, such processes have been steered into powerful biotechnologies for energy production in bioreactors. Decoding the functional and taxonomic landscape of these communities requires comprehensive surveys, including bacteriophages and plasmids, which, however, remain vastly underrepresented in current databases. Here, we present the microbial Catalogue of Anaerobic Digestion (CAnDi), a database comprising
papers.summary: CAnDi is a new global database that catalogues the microbiomes involved in anaerobic digestion, including bacteria, archaea, bacteriophages, and plasmids. It addresses the underrepresentation of these communities in existing databases, providing a comprehensive resource for studying methane-producing consortia in both natural and engineered environments.

papers.title: Influence of Gliricidia sepium living support on rhizosphere bacterial recruitment and fruit metabolomics in black pepper (Piper nigrum).
papers.abstract: The ability of the rhizosphere to recruit beneficial microorganisms is central to the sustainable management of crops. Here, we investigated, through shotgun metagenomic sequencing and mass spectrometry techniques, the microbial composition, antimicrobial resistance (AMRs), and metabolomic profiles of Piper nigrum cultivated under two support systems: living Gliricidia sepium support (SL/RL) and dead wooden support (SD/RD). Bulk and rhizosphere soils were sequenced to assess taxonomic structure and ARGs, with emphasis on Actinobacteria due to their relevance in antibiotic production. Actinobac
papers.summary: This study compared the rhizosphere microbiome and fruit metabolome of black pepper grown on living Gliricidia sepium support trees versus dead wooden stakes, using shotgun metagenomics and mass spectrometry. Living support altered bacterial recruitment in the rhizosphere, with particular attention to Actinobacteria and antimicrobial resistance genes, and was associated with differences in fruit metabolite profiles. The work suggests that living support systems can shape beneficial microbial recruitment and crop chemistry.

papers.title: Assembly of minimally fragmented metagenomic pangenome graphs.
papers.abstract: Pangenome variation graphs are a powerful tool for representing genetic diversity within and across populations. For comparative and evolutionary genomic analyses leveraging these graph-based structures, it is important that graph topology reflects the underlying phylogenetic and genetic similarities of the genomes embedded within the graph. However, in metagenomic settings these approaches often produce highly fragmented multi-component graphs, hindering comparisons of genomes embedded across different components. This challenge is particularly pronounced for hypervariable viral families like
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint addresses the problem of fragmented pangenome variation graphs in metagenomic settings, where highly variable viral families produce multi-component graphs that hinder comparative and evolutionary analyses. The authors propose an assembly approach that minimizes fragmentation, aiming to keep genomes embedded within a single connected graph component so that graph topology better reflects underlying phylogenetic and genetic similarity.

papers.title: Network perturbation of lactate metabolism identifies an aggressive hepatocellular carcinoma subtype with distinct immune and microbial features.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) exhibits significant heterogeneity, and the reprogramming of lactate metabolism (LM) plays a crucial role in tumor progression and immune evasion. Classification based on perturbations in the gene interaction network related to LM may reveal new molecular subtypes. This study aimed to construct an LM interaction perturbation-based classification of HCC and to characterize the clinical, immune, and intratumoral microbial features of the identified subtypes.
papers.summary: This study classifies hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) into molecular subtypes based on perturbations in the gene interaction network of lactate metabolism, rather than expression levels alone. The authors identify an aggressive subtype with distinct immune and intratumoral microbial features, suggesting that network-based classification can reveal clinically relevant heterogeneity in HCC.

papers.title: Senimuribacter muris sp. nov., a butyrate-producing bacterium isolated from mouse feces, and reclassification of members of the family Eubacteriaceae into the family Anaerovoracaceae.
papers.abstract: Two strictly anaerobic, Gram-stain-positive, non-motile, and rod-shaped bacterial strains, designated rT4E-8T and mB4P-1, were isolated from the feces of specific-pathogen-free Mus musculus (C57BL/6J). Both strains were catalase- and oxidase-negative and produced butyrate as a major fermentation product, with optimal growth at 37 °C and pH 7. The two strains shared 100% pairwise 16S rRNA gene sequence similarity and showed high similarity to Senimuribacter intestinalis DSM 106208T (95.1-95.3%). Genome sizes of strains rT4E-8T and mB4P-1 were 2.9 Mbp and 2.8 Mbp, with genomic DNA G+C contents o
papers.summary: The authors describe two new bacterial strains isolated from mouse feces that produce butyrate, a short-chain fatty acid important for gut health. Based on genetic and phenotypic comparisons, they propose a new species, Senimuribacter muris, and also reclassify members of the family Eubacteriaceae into the family Anaerovoracaceae.

papers.title: Microencapsulated immunoglobulin Y and lactic acid bacteria improve intestinal health in Yanbian Yellow calves.
papers.abstract: Neonatal calf diarrhea remains a major cause of morbidity and growth impairment, highlighting the need for stable and effective antibiotic alternatives that can simultaneously suppress enteric pathogens and improve gut health. We aimed to develop microcapsules containing immunoglobulin Y (IgY) and mixed lactic acid bacteria (LAB), termed IgY-LAB-MCs, and to evaluate their efficacy and optimal dosage as an alternative strategy for preventing calf diarrhea.
papers.summary: This study developed microcapsules containing immunoglobulin Y (IgY) and mixed lactic acid bacteria (IgY-LAB-MCs) as an antibiotic alternative to prevent neonatal calf diarrhea. The researchers evaluated the efficacy and optimal dosage of these microcapsules in Yanbian Yellow calves, finding that they improved intestinal health by suppressing enteric pathogens and enhancing gut function. The work supports microencapsulated IgY-LAB as a stable, effective strategy for reducing diarrhea-related morbidity and growth impairment in calves.

papers.title: An integrated in vitro gastrointestinal digestion and fermentation model as a complementary tool for evaluating feed ingredients in young broilers: a case study with peas.
papers.abstract: The search for sustainable protein sources in broiler nutrition has increased interest in locally produced ingredients such as peas. However, nutritional evaluation of alternative feed ingredients relies on costly and ethically constrained animal trials, while standardized in vitro models representing the complete gastrointestinal tract of young broilers are lacking. These models should reflect their lower digestive capacity and less complex caecal microbiota. This study developed an innovative in vitro model simulating the complete gastrointestinal tract of young broilers and used peas as a c
papers.summary: This study developed an integrated in vitro model that simulates the complete gastrointestinal tract of young broilers, including digestion and caecal fermentation, to evaluate feed ingredients without animal trials. Using peas as a case study, the model captures the lower digestive capacity and simpler caecal microbiota characteristic of young birds. It offers a complementary, ethically favorable tool for screening alternative protein sources in poultry nutrition.

papers.title: Advances in 16S Taxonomic Classification: Impacts on Species-Level Resolution of Female Bladder Microbiota.
papers.abstract: Bacteria are present in the human urinary bladder, even in the absence of infection. These bacteria comprise the urinary microbiome, or urobiome, and have the potential to promote bladder health or contribute to pathology. Despite its importance, studying the urobiome remains challenging given the high proportion of host to bacterial cells and low microbial biomass. The leading method for studying the urobiome has been 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing. This culture-independent approach provides a cost-effective method for identifying bacteria, but taxonomic classification accuracy depends on three
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint examines how advances in 16S rRNA taxonomic classification methods affect species-level resolution of the female bladder microbiome (urobiome). Because the urobiome is a low-biomass community with high host-to-bacterial DNA ratios, classification accuracy is especially challenging, and the authors assess how newer taxonomic tools and reference databases influence species-level assignments. The work highlights that methodological choices in 16S classification can materially change the inferred composition of the bladder microbiota.

papers.title: Multikingdom and functional gut microbiota markers for cholangiocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: While the association between gut microbiota and cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) has been explored, existing research has been limited to bacterial components. The alterations in non-bacterial members (fungi, archaea, and viruses) and their functional characteristics in CCA remain unclear. This study aimed to comprehensively characterize the multi-kingdom gut microbiota and functional profiles in CCA patients and develop a non-invasive diagnostic model.
papers.summary: This study moves beyond bacteria to characterize fungi, archaea, and viruses in the gut microbiota of cholangiocarcinoma patients, along with functional profiles. The authors use these multikingdom and functional markers to build a non-invasive diagnostic model for CCA.

papers.title: Shifts in the Maternal Gut Microbiome Across Pregnancy are Associated with Energetic Status in Phayre's Leaf Monkeys.
papers.abstract: During pregnancy, mothers experience physiological changes that support fetal development, including shifts in energy utilization and increasing insulin resistance during late gestation. While these changes benefit the fetus, they can also impose energetic costs that affect the mother's physical condition and metabolic phenotype. Previous studies suggest that the gut microbiome, a key regulator of female metabolism and energy harvest, may play a critical role in mediating these physiological challenges.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study examines how the gut microbiome of pregnant Phayre's leaf monkeys changes across gestation and whether those changes relate to the mother's energetic condition. The authors find that microbiome shifts during pregnancy are associated with maternal energetic status, suggesting the microbiome may help mediate the metabolic demands of gestation. The work extends microbiome–pregnancy links from humans and lab models to a wild primate.

papers.title: Disrupted microbial queuosine biosynthesis contributes to dysbiosis in human inflammatory bowel disease.
papers.abstract: As a microbiome/diet-derived vitamin, queuine (q) is a micronutrient that eukaryotes acquire from microbiota or diet. Vitamin q, the free base form of queuosine (Q), is used for Q-modification of transfer RNA (tRNA). Although tRNA-Q-modification in regulating eukaryotic cell physiology is recognized, the relationship between Q-tRNA-modification and the human microbiome in health and inflammatory bowel diseases (IBD) remains unknown. Which bacteria produce q and how the q-producing bacteria contributing to human health and IBD are not explored. Here, we hypothesize that disrupted microbial Q-bi
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: This preprint proposes that bacteria in the gut microbiome produce queuine (q), a vitamin-like molecule used to modify tRNA in host cells, and that disruption of microbial queuosine biosynthesis contributes to dysbiosis in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). The authors frame the work around the unexplored link between bacterial q production, tRNA-Q modification, and human health versus IBD, though the abstract is truncated and does not report specific results.

papers.title: Scellmate enables contamination aware curation and host mobilome linkage analysis of large SAG datasets.
papers.abstract: Single-cell genomics enables cell-resolved insights into in-situ microbial communities, yet single amplified genomes (SAGs) are often fragmented, taxonomically ambiguous, and prone to contamination, limiting their biological interpretation. Here, we present Scellmate, a scalable, semi-supervised framework that integrates whole-SAG curation, species-level taxonomic anchoring and SAG-mobilome linkage analysis for large-scale SAG datasets. Following benchmarking of its SAG curation and SAG-eMGE linkage modules using in silico and four-strain mock SAG datasets, respectively, Scellmate was applied
papers.summary: Scellmate is a scalable semi-supervised framework for curating large single-amplified genome (SAG) datasets, addressing fragmentation, taxonomic ambiguity, and contamination that limit biological interpretation. It integrates whole-SAG curation, species-level taxonomic anchoring, and SAG-mobilome linkage analysis, and was benchmarked on in silico and mock SAG datasets before application to real data. The tool enables contamination-aware analysis and links SAGs to mobile genetic elements, improving cell-resolved study of microbial communities.

papers.title: Elevated Level of Fannyhessea vaginae Correlated with Implantation Outcomes in Women undergoing in vitro fertilization Treatment.
papers.abstract: The vaginal microbiome plays a significant role in reproductive health. While maintaining a balanced vaginal microbiome is crucial for successful in vitro fertilization (IVF) outcomes, the specific bacteria associated with adverse outcomes may vary by region and are largely unknown. This study aims to investigate the bacterial profiles and their influence on embryo implantation, thereby supporting the development of microbiome-based therapies. One hundred women undergoing IVF provided vaginal swabs at three stages: oocyte retrieval, embryo transfer, and hCG pregnancy testing. An in-house 16S r
papers.summary: This study profiled the vaginal microbiome of 100 women undergoing IVF at three timepoints (oocyte retrieval, embryo transfer, and pregnancy testing) using 16S rRNA sequencing and linked bacterial composition to embryo implantation outcomes. Elevated levels of Fannyhessea vaginae were associated with poorer implantation outcomes, suggesting this species may serve as a marker or target for microbiome-based interventions to improve IVF success.

papers.title: An antibiotic-treated mouse model reveals the progression of intestinal botulism.
papers.abstract: Intestinal botulism, including infant botulism and adult intestinal toxemia botulism, is a life-threatening disease caused by intestinal infection with Clostridium botulinum (Cb) spores. Infants are particularly susceptible to Cb infection because of their immature gut microbiota, whereas healthy adults are generally protected by gut microbiota-mediated colonization resistance. Thus, immature gut microbiota or gut dysbiosis is thought to permit Cb colonization. However, the mechanisms underlying colonization resistance and disease progression remain poorly characterized. Here, using adult mice
papers.summary: This study establishes an antibiotic-treated adult mouse model of intestinal botulism, showing that disrupting the gut microbiota allows Clostridium botulinum spores to colonize the intestine and cause disease. The model provides a tractable system for dissecting how gut microbiota-mediated colonization resistance normally prevents Cb infection and how disease progresses once that barrier is lost.

papers.title: Temperature effects on life history strategies for rapid growth potential of leaf epiphytic bacteria.
papers.abstract: Phyllosphere bacteria, occupying both epiphytic and endophytic habitats, constitute a critical plant-atmosphere interface. However, their community assembly and life-history strategies (LHSs) in response to temperature increase remain poorly understood. Here, we compared leaf phyllosphere bacterial communities with those in other plant compartments across four representative plant species from an alpine meadow on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau. By combining observations along an elevational gradient with a controlled warming experiment, we found that temperature was closely associated with the dete
papers.summary: This study examined how temperature shapes the life-history strategies of leaf-dwelling (epiphytic) bacteria in alpine meadow plants on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau, combining an elevational gradient survey with a controlled warming experiment. Temperature was closely linked to the composition and assembly of phyllosphere bacterial communities, with warming favoring bacteria with rapid-growth life-history strategies. The work highlights the plant-atmosphere interface as a sensitive zone for microbial community shifts under climate warming.

papers.title: Identification of ebastine and ceritinib as effective inhibitors of Fusobacterium nucleatum FtsZ.
papers.abstract: The role of microorganisms in cancer is not a new concept-bacteria, parasites, and viruses have all been implicated in cancer development. Fusobacterium nucleatum, a member of the oral microbiota, has emerged as an important cancer-associated bacterium. Unbiased global genomic analyses have demonstrated that F. nucleatum is enriched in human colorectal cancer (CRC) tissues compared with noncancerous colorectal tissues, underscoring the urgent need for specific antimicrobial agents targeting F. nucleatum for CRC prevention and treatment. In this study, structure-based virtual screening successf
papers.summary: The authors used structure-based virtual screening to identify existing drugs ebastine and ceritinib as inhibitors of FtsZ, an essential cell-division protein in the cancer-associated bacterium Fusobacterium nucleatum. These compounds could serve as starting points for antimicrobials aimed at reducing F. nucleatum enrichment in colorectal cancer tissues.

papers.title: The protection of chronic cerebral ischemia by Hua-Feng-Dan involves the modulation of hippocampal transcriptome and gut dysbiosis.
papers.abstract: The protective effects of Hua-Feng-Dan recipes against chronic cerebral hypoperfusion-induced ischemia were examined; RNA-seq and 16 S-rRNA-seq were used to explore the molecular mechanisms. Male Sprague-Dawley rats underwent unilateral common carotid artery ligation surgery to establish chronic cerebral hypoperfusion (CCH) models. Then, the CCH rats were treated with various Hua-Feng-Dan recipes in diet for 20 days. Finally, behavioral tests were performed, followed by histopathology. Hippocampal RNA was isolated for RNA-seq and RT-qPCR analyses; Colon bacterial DNA was isolated for 16 S rRNA
papers.summary: This study investigated whether Hua-Feng-Dan, a traditional Chinese medicine formula, protects against chronic cerebral hypoperfusion (a model of chronic cerebral ischemia) in rats. Using hippocampal RNA-seq and 16S rRNA sequencing of gut bacteria, the authors linked the treatment's protective effects on behavior and brain histopathology to changes in hippocampal gene expression and gut microbiome composition. The work suggests that Hua-Feng-Dan's neuroprotection may be mediated through modulation of both the hippocampal transcriptome and gut dysbiosis.

papers.title: Children at risk of vitamin A deficiency exhibit taxonomic dysbiosis and functional remodeling of the gut microbiome: a matched case-control study.
papers.abstract: Vitamin A deficiency is one of the most prevalent micronutrient deficiencies worldwide. This condition increases susceptibility to infections and due to its role in intestinal barrier integrity, it has been suggested that it could predispose to gut dysbiosis.
papers.summary: This matched case-control study examines whether children at risk of vitamin A deficiency show altered gut microbiome composition and function. The authors report taxonomic dysbiosis and functional remodeling of the gut microbiome in at-risk children, suggesting a link between vitamin A status and microbiome ecology. The findings support the hypothesis that vitamin A deficiency may predispose children to gut dysbiosis, with potential implications for infection susceptibility.

papers.title: Integrated optimization of experimental and computational workflows improves genome recovery in long-read gut metagenomics.
papers.abstract: Short-read metagenomic sequencing has been widely applied in microbial research due to its high quality and decreasing cost. However, short reads are inherently fragmented, which limits assembly contiguity and the recovery of complete microbial genomes. In contrast, long-read sequencing, with significantly longer read lengths, helps overcome these limitations. Achieving complete and accurate genome recovery is the core goal of metagenomics. To address this challenge, we systematically evaluated and optimized the long-read metagenomic workflow, from sample processing to computational assembly,
papers.summary: This study systematically evaluated and optimized a long-read metagenomic workflow, from sample processing through computational assembly, to improve recovery of complete microbial genomes from gut microbiome samples. The integrated optimization of experimental and computational steps yields better genome recovery than standard approaches, addressing the fragmentation limits of short-read sequencing.

papers.title: Sex influences the mosquito virome in a host-specific way.
papers.abstract: Mosquitoes harbor diverse eukaryotic viruses. These viral communities, or viromes, probably influence mosquito physiology, including pathogen transmission. However, the factors shaping the virome remain largely unstudied, limiting our understanding of its role in mosquito biology. Here, we assess the influence of sex on the eukaryotic virome of mosquitoes. Ecological differences between males and females, such as female-specific blood feeding, may lead to differential viral exposure and virome structure. We investigated the influence of sex in sympatric populations of Culex quinquefasciatus an
papers.summary: This study investigates how mosquito sex shapes the eukaryotic virome in sympatric populations of Culex quinquefasciatus. The authors find that sex influences virome composition in a host-specific manner, likely reflecting ecological differences such as female-specific blood feeding that alter viral exposure. These results highlight sex as an important factor structuring mosquito viral communities, with potential implications for pathogen transmission.

papers.title: Diversity and evolution of the ribovirian class Stelpaviricetes.
papers.abstract: Metatranscriptome mining has dramatically expanded the known diversity of ribovirians at all taxonomic levels. We explored the class Stelpaviricetes in the phylum Pisuviricota that currently includes three orders and six recognized virus families: order Stellavirales with family Astroviridae infecting vertebrates; Patatavirales with families Potyviridae, the largest known family of plant ribovirians, and Potyliviridae; and Hypofuvirales consisting of three families of viruses associated largely with phytopathogenic fungi. Using an order-specific collection of Hidden Markov Model profiles for t
papers.summary: This study uses metatranscriptome mining with order-specific Hidden Markov Models to explore the diversity and evolution of the ribovirian class Stelpaviricetes, which includes vertebrate-infecting astroviruses, plant potyviruses, and fungus-associated viruses. The work substantially expands the known taxonomic diversity within this class and provides insights into its evolutionary relationships.

papers.title: Physiological, behavioral, and genetic factors that shape interactions in the plant growth-promoting maize rhizosphere synthetic community.
papers.abstract: Profiling microbiomes is an important way to understand the function and composition of communities in the wild, but natural microbiomes are often highly complex and often unamenable to experimentation to reveal cause-and-effect relationships. By using a small group of cultivable strains to represent those found in the wild, synthetic communities are one solution to this problem. Here we describe the maize rhizosphere synthetic community (MARSc), a genome-enabled 31-member bacterial community representative of the diversity found on the roots of maize grown in Iowa soils. This community is bui
papers.summary: The authors describe MARSc, a genome-enabled synthetic community of 31 bacterial strains representative of the maize rhizosphere in Iowa soils. By combining genomic, physiological, and behavioral profiling, they identify factors that shape interactions among community members, providing a tractable system for dissecting cause-and-effect relationships in plant-microbiome research.

papers.title: Exploring normality: Mapping the endometrial microbiome in healthy reproductive-aged women from Argentina.
papers.abstract: The human microbiome varies according to individual and geographic characteristics. The endometrial microbiome plays a relevant role in reproductive physiology; however, data from healthy South American populations remain scarce. This prospective observational study aimed to characterize the endometrial microbiome in healthy reproductive-aged women from Rosario, Argentina and to establish a regional baseline for future research. A total of 100 healthy women aged 22-50 years from Rosario, Argentina, were included. Endometrial samples were obtained by aspiration biopsy during the follicular phas
papers.summary: This prospective observational study characterized the endometrial microbiome of 100 healthy reproductive-aged women in Rosario, Argentina, using aspiration biopsies during the follicular phase. It provides a regional baseline for the endometrial microbiome in a South American population, where such data were previously scarce. The findings help define what constitutes a 'normal' endometrial microbiome in this geographic context.

papers.title: Monitoring single-cell metabolic phenotyping changes of Daqu microbiota during fermentation by Raman spectroscopy.
papers.abstract: Monitoring microbial community dynamics during natural food fermentation is essential for stabilizing fermentation processes and improving product flavor profiles. This study employed single-cell Raman spectroscopy to monitor the metabolic change of Daqu microbiota during fermentation. First, we developed an operational phenotypic unit (OPU)-based clustering method to process Raman spectral data of a nine-member microbial community. The clustering was validated by sorting out representative single cells from different OPUs and performing 16S/ITS region sequencing. Second, single-cell Raman spe
papers.summary: This study applies single-cell Raman spectroscopy to track metabolic phenotype changes in the microbial community of Daqu, a traditional fermentation starter, over the course of fermentation. The authors introduce an 'operational phenotypic unit' (OPU)-based clustering method for Raman spectra and validate it by sequencing representative single cells via 16S/ITS regions. The work demonstrates that single-cell metabolic phenotyping can resolve community dynamics during natural food fermentation.

papers.title: Scaffold-level validation is needed for phage-host inference from metagenome-assembled genomes.
papers.abstract: Accurate phage-host prediction underpins ecological interpretation and experimental validation of uncultivated phages, yet most current approaches rely heavily on metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs). This reliance implicitly assumes that MAG-level quality metrics, such as completeness and contamination, ensure scaffold-level correctness. Here, we demonstrate that this assumption can be violated under particular challenging conditions. Tetranucleotide frequency (TNF) analyses reveal that CRISPR-associated regions often diverge compositionally from their host genomes, increasing the risk of misb
papers.summary: This paper argues that current phage-host prediction methods relying on metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) may be unreliable because MAG-level quality metrics do not guarantee scaffold-level correctness. Using tetranucleotide frequency analyses, the authors show that CRISPR-associated regions can differ compositionally from their host genomes, increasing the risk of misassigning phage-host relationships. They call for scaffold-level validation to improve the accuracy of phage-host inference.

papers.title: Molecular mechanisms of colorectal cancer: from carcinogenesis and molecular classification to targeted therapy.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a heterogeneous disease that results from the progressive accumulation and interactions at multiple levels of genetic alterations, which lead to the transformation of normal colonic epithelium into malignant colorectal tumors. Understanding the molecular basis of CRC pathogenesis, together with the interactions between genetic alterations, epigenetic modifications, environmental and lifestyle factors, is essential for improving prevention, diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment strategies. This review aims to provide a critical reference point for understanding the temp
papers.summary: This review synthesizes the molecular mechanisms underlying colorectal cancer, covering the stepwise genetic and epigenetic alterations that drive carcinogenesis, the molecular classification of CRC subtypes, and how these insights inform targeted therapy. It emphasizes the interplay between genetic changes, epigenetic modifications, and environmental/lifestyle factors in shaping prevention, diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment strategies.

papers.title: Optimized Super-SILAC Normalization Enables Enhanced Profiling of Histone Post-Translational Modification Changes Associated with Microbiota and Acute Inflammation.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiota produces metabolites, such as short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) that modulate histone acylation and serve as precursors for non-acetyl acyl marks, representing a mechanism in host-microbiome epigenetic crosstalk. However, the reliable quantification of these low-abundance modifications in complex tissues remains challenging. Here, we established an optimized, non-acetyl histone acylation-focused super-SILAC strategy for profiling histone post-translational modifications (HPTM) in the gut epithelium. We generated a functionally optimized internal standard from heavy-labeled col
papers.summary: This paper develops an optimized super-SILAC (stable isotope labeling by amino acids in cell culture) strategy specifically for quantifying low-abundance non-acetyl histone acylation marks in gut epithelial tissue. The method uses a heavy-labeled internal standard to improve reliable profiling of histone post-translational modifications linked to microbiota-derived metabolites like short-chain fatty acids and acute inflammation. It enables better detection of host-microbiome epigenetic crosstalk that was previously difficult to measure in complex tissues.

papers.title: Shotgun metagenomic characterization of human adenovirus F40 and a non-cpe Clostridium perfringens strain in pediatric prolonged diarrhea: a genome-resolved case study.
papers.abstract: Viral and bacterial pathogens may be concurrently detected in pediatric gastroenteritis, yet such findings are often missed by routine diagnostic methods. Shotgun metagenomic sequencing enables comprehensive detection and genomic characterization of microorganisms present in clinical specimens, including pathogens that may not be recovered by conventional testing.
papers.summary: This case study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to characterize human adenovirus F40 and a non-cpe Clostridium perfringens strain in a pediatric patient with prolonged diarrhea. The work demonstrates that metagenomics can detect and genomically characterize multiple pathogens missed by routine diagnostics, highlighting its value for complex gastroenteritis cases.

papers.title: Genome-resolved taxonomy, global distribution, and EPS potential of Zoogloea, the canonical floc-former in wastewater treatment systems.
papers.abstract: The bacterial genus Zoogloea is the fourth most abundant genus in wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) globally, where it plays key roles in floc formation and nutrient removal but can also contribute to viscous bulking when highly abundant. The taxonomic assignment of Zoogloea has historically been inconsistent, as several taxa were classified based on phenotypic characteristics and later reassigned to other families or orders. This has obscured both the identity and distribution of Zoogloea and hindered interpretation of its floc-forming mechanisms, which have been attributed to polysaccharid
papers.summary: This study uses genome-resolved taxonomy to clarify the classification of Zoogloea, the fourth most abundant bacterial genus in wastewater treatment plants globally, resolving historical inconsistencies in its taxonomic assignment. It maps the global distribution of Zoogloea and examines its potential for producing extracellular polymeric substances (EPS), which drive floc formation and can cause viscous bulking. The work provides a clearer framework for understanding this key floc-former's identity and ecological roles in WWTPs.

papers.title: Reciprocity between the intestinal microbiome and urobiome in children with and without urinary tract infection: protocol of a single-centre, nested case-control study in Denmark.
papers.summary: This paper presents a study protocol for a single-centre nested case-control study in Denmark investigating the bidirectional relationship between the gut microbiome and the urinary microbiome (urobiome) in children with and without urinary tract infection (UTI). The protocol outlines methods for sampling and analyzing both microbial communities to determine whether alterations in one niche are associated with UTI status and with changes in the other. As a protocol, it does not report results but sets up a framework to test reciprocity between these two microbiomes in a pediatric population.

papers.title: Global Carriage of Antimicrobial Resistance Genes and Virulence Factors Among Physicians in Cirrhosis Care.
papers.abstract: Cirrhosis patients are at high risk for drug-resistant infections, which may be transmitted between patients and healthcare providers. In this study, we used shotgun metagenomics to characterize the fecal microbiome of physicians in cirrhosis care (n = 55) across 9 countries. Our results indicate physicians from low- or middle-income countries carry greater antimicrobial resistance gene (ARG) diversity corresponding to increased taxonomic richness. Physicians carried a low prevalence of clinically relevant ARGs or virulence factors (VFs), regardless of country of practice or patient exposure.
papers.summary: Using shotgun metagenomics on fecal samples from 55 physicians in cirrhosis care across 9 countries, the study found that physicians in low- and middle-income countries carried greater antimicrobial resistance gene diversity, which tracked with overall taxonomic richness. However, clinically relevant resistance genes and virulence factors were rare regardless of country or patient exposure, suggesting limited occupational acquisition of high-risk determinants.

papers.title: Importance of rumen ciliated protozoa and current research techniques for their analysis.
papers.abstract: Rumen protozoa are an integral component of the ruminant foregut microbiome, with a profound influence on feed digestion, microbial ecosystem dynamics and enteric methane emissions. Although they represent only a small proportion of species richness, protozoa contribute significantly to microbial biomass and functions in fibre degradation, volatile fatty acid production, microbial protein turnover, pH modulation and hydrogen-mediated methanogenesis. In addition to highlighting their importance to rumen function, this review summarizes classical and contemporary methodologies for enumerating, i
papers.summary: This review highlights the outsized role of ciliated protozoa in the rumen microbiome, despite their low species richness, in fibre digestion, volatile fatty acid production, microbial protein turnover, pH regulation and hydrogen-driven methane production. It also surveys classical and modern methods for enumerating and analysing these protozoa, making the case for renewed attention to this often-overlooked microbial group.

papers.title: Infective endocarditis due to a novel Gemella species revealed by metagenomic sequencing.
papers.abstract: Gemella species are rare causes of infective endocarditis, and accurate species identification can be challenging with routine diagnostic methods. We report infective endocarditis caused by a novel Gemella species, highlighting the diagnostic value of sequencing-based approaches for bacteria not registered in public databases and the risk of misclassification when novel species are not represented in reference databases.
papers.summary: This case report describes a patient with infective endocarditis caused by a previously unknown Gemella species, identified through metagenomic sequencing after routine diagnostic methods failed to classify it accurately. The case highlights how sequencing-based approaches can detect novel pathogens absent from public reference databases, and warns that such gaps can lead to misclassification.

papers.title: Benchmarking nanopore-based strategies for antimicrobial resistance prediction.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) presents a pressing need to ensure that the right antimicrobials are used to target the right microbes at the right time. Ideally, the appropriate antimicrobial is selected after patient samples have been cultured and assessed with antimicrobial sensitivity testing (AST). However, the time needed for culture-based diagnosis leads to immediate empirical treatment, often with broad-spectrum and/or high-tier antimicrobials. Direct nanopore metagenomic whole-genome sequencing to identify pathogens and predict their AMR is a rapid and patient-side alternative. A limit
papers.summary: This study benchmarks different nanopore sequencing strategies for predicting antimicrobial resistance directly from patient samples, aiming to bypass the slow culture-based diagnostics that force broad-spectrum empirical treatment. It evaluates trade-offs between speed and accuracy in metagenomic whole-genome sequencing approaches for rapid, patient-side AMR prediction.

papers.title: Seasonal and Environmental Influences on Microbial Community Dynamics in the Dunk River Watershed, Prince Edward Island, Canada.
papers.abstract: Riverine ecosystems are crucial biogeochemical hubs, with their microbial communities playing a key role in nutrient cycling and overall ecosystem health. This study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to characterize the seasonal and environmental drivers of taxonomic and functional microbial community structure (read depth between 1.91 and 30.44 bp) in four tributaries of the Dunk River watershed in Prince Edward Island (PEI), a landscape shaped by intensive agriculture and groundwater-dominated streamflow, where the seasonal and land-use impacts on the river's microbiome remain understudied
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to characterize how seasonal and environmental factors shape microbial community composition and function across four tributaries of the Dunk River watershed in Prince Edward Island, a region dominated by intensive agriculture and groundwater-fed streams. The work identifies seasonal and land-use drivers of riverine microbiome structure in an understudied agricultural watershed.

papers.title: Planetary-scale metagenomic analysis reveals CRISPR targeting dynamics across ecosystems.
papers.abstract: Interactions between microorganisms and their mobile genetic elements (MGEs), including viruses and plasmids, impact microbiome dynamics. CRISPR-Cas systems are important regulators of these host-MGE interactions, but a global understanding of the diversity, activity and roles of CRISPR spacers across Earth's biomes is still lacking. Here we develop a computational approach to search short-read data and collect 794 million CRISPR spacers across 367,609 public metagenomes, from which we identified 1.18 billion hits between 41 million spacers and 2.5 million viruses and plasmids. While spacers w
papers.summary: This study develops a computational pipeline to mine CRISPR spacers from short-read metagenomic data, yielding 794 million spacers from 367,609 public metagenomes. By matching spacers to mobile genetic elements, the authors identified 1.18 billion spacer–virus/plasmid interactions, providing a planetary-scale view of CRISPR targeting dynamics across ecosystems. The work establishes a large resource for studying host–MGE interactions in microbiomes.

papers.title: Strong agreement in absolute marine prokaryote abundance from epifluorescence microscopy and internal-standard-corrected metagenomics.
papers.abstract: Quantifying microbial cell abundance in natural environments with taxonomic resolution remains a central challenge in microbial ecology. While epifluorescence microscopy reliably enumerates free-living cells, it lacks taxonomic specificity and is less suitable for quantifying cells in sediments, soils, and on surfaces. Furthermore, most omics approaches profile microbial communities, but they typically provide only relative abundances. Recent advances in quantitative metagenomics using single-copy marker genes and genomic internal standards enable taxon-specific abundance estimates in absolute
papers.summary: This study compares absolute abundance estimates of marine prokaryotes obtained by traditional epifluorescence microscopy with those from a quantitative metagenomics approach that uses genomic internal standards and single-copy marker genes. The two methods showed strong agreement, supporting internal-standard-corrected metagenomics as a reliable way to obtain taxon-specific absolute cell abundances directly from environmental samples. This is valuable because microscopy cannot resolve taxonomy or easily handle sediments and surfaces, while standard omics methods give only relative abundances.

papers.title: Cross hybridization inference for phylogenetic resolution-fluorescence in situ hybridization enables microbiome imaging with strain level taxonomic resolution.
papers.abstract: The spatial organization of microbial communities is a critical determinant of host-microbe interactions, yet species-level mapping remains challenging due to high 16S rRNA sequence homology and spectral crosstalk in multiplexed fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH). To address this challenge, we developed Cross-hybridization Inference for Phylogenetic Resolution (CIPHR)-FISH, a pipeline that integrates strategic probe design with supervised machine learning. CIPHR-FISH transforms probe cross-hybridization, traditionally viewed as experimental noise, into informative molecular signatures.
papers.summary: The authors present CIPHR-FISH, a pipeline that combines strategic probe design with supervised machine learning to turn probe cross-hybridization—normally treated as noise—into a useful signal for resolving closely related microbes. This enables multiplexed FISH imaging of microbiomes at strain-level taxonomic resolution, addressing the challenge of high 16S rRNA homology and spectral crosstalk.

papers.title: Gut‒liver‒brain axis signature of cirrhosis-related cognitive impairment is consistent across multi-national cohorts.
papers.abstract: Cognitive impairment in cirrhosis is associated with an altered gut‒liver‒brain axis, but geographic variations in diet and clinical practices may limit generalizability. We investigated consistency of microbial signatures for cirrhosis-related cognitive impairment across four countries. We enrolled outpatients with cirrhosis from USA, Denmark, Lithuania, and Mexico who underwent Psychometric Hepatic Encephalopathy Score (PHES) testing for covert hepatic encephalopathy (CHE), and stool shotgun metagenomic sequencing. Taxonomic and functional associations with PHES were evaluated after adjustme
papers.summary: This study examined whether gut microbiome signatures associated with cognitive impairment in cirrhosis are consistent across patients from four countries (USA, Denmark, Lithuania, Mexico). Using stool shotgun metagenomic sequencing and PHES testing for covert hepatic encephalopathy, they found that taxonomic and functional microbial associations with cognitive scores were reproducible across the multi-national cohorts despite differences in diet and clinical practice. This supports a generalizable gut‒liver‒brain axis signature for cirrhosis-related cognitive impairment.

papers.title: Metagenomic characterization of gut microbiota in patients with Disorders of Gut-Brain Interaction.
papers.abstract: Patients with Disorders of Gut-Brain Interaction (DGBI) experience recurrent gastrointestinal symptoms without identifiable organic abnormalities. While earlier studies focused on neural and hormonal regulation, recent evidence suggests that gut microbiota dysbiosis and altered microbial metabolism may play key roles in DGBI.
papers.summary: This study uses metagenomic sequencing to characterize the gut microbiota composition and functional potential in patients with Disorders of Gut-Brain Interaction (DGBI), a group of chronic gastrointestinal conditions without clear organic cause. The authors compare microbial profiles between DGBI patients and controls, identifying dysbiosis patterns and metabolic pathway differences that may contribute to symptom generation via the microbiota-gut-brain axis.

papers.title: Metagenomic analysis of tomato rhizosphere microbiomes detects Ralstonia phage sequences in Kenyan agricultural soils.
papers.abstract: Bacterial wilt caused by Ralstonia solanacearum species complex is a major constraint in tomato production in Kenya, resulting in yield losses of up to 100% in heavily infested fields. This study used high-throughput shotgun metagenomic sequencing approach to characterize the rhizosphere microbiomes of tomato plants in three of the major production areas in Kenya (Kirinyaga, Kiambu, and Laikipia counties) focusing on detecting Ralstonia phage sequences. Soil samples were collected from the rhizosphere of bacterial wilt-infected tomato plants, and microbial DNA was extracted using a modified ph
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to characterize tomato rhizosphere microbiomes from three major tomato-producing regions in Kenya, with a focus on detecting Ralstonia phage sequences in bacterial wilt-infected fields. The work provides a survey of rhizosphere microbial communities in Kenyan agricultural soils and identifies phage sequences associated with Ralstonia solanacearum, the pathogen causing bacterial wilt. This establishes a baseline for exploring phage-based biocontrol strategies against this devastating tomato disease.

papers.title: A systematic review of the effects of diet on the gut microbiota in individuals at elevated risk for colorectal cancer.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) poses a major public health concern, with emerging evidence highlighting the critical role of the gut microbiota in CRC progression. Considering that diet is a major modifiable factor influencing CRC risk, partly through its interaction with the gut microbiome, this systematic review evaluated the effects of dietary intervention RCTs, including supplements, functional foods, whole foods, and dietary patterns, on the gut microbiome in elevated-risk individuals.
papers.summary: This systematic review examines randomized controlled trials of dietary interventions—including supplements, functional foods, whole foods, and dietary patterns—and their effects on the gut microbiome in people at elevated risk for colorectal cancer. It synthesizes evidence on how diet, a modifiable CRC risk factor, may influence CRC risk through microbiome interactions. The review aims to clarify which dietary strategies show measurable microbiome effects in this high-risk population.

papers.title: Co-occurrence and genetic contexts of NDM-1, KPC-2, IMP-1, and AFM-1 carbapenemase genes in a critically ill patient.
papers.abstract: Carbapenem-resistant organisms are increasingly reported in clinical settings, yet the simultaneous detection of multiple carbapenemase genes within a single specimen remains rare.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This case report describes the simultaneous detection of four distinct carbapenemase genes (NDM-1, KPC-2, IMP-1, and AFM-1) in a single critically ill patient, an unusually complex resistance profile. The study characterizes the co-occurrence and genetic contexts of these genes, highlighting the potential for horizontal gene transfer and the diagnostic challenges posed by multi-carbapenemase-producing organisms.

papers.title: Why does apical periodontitis persist? A shotgun metagenomic survey of the microbial community in primary and persistent periapical granulomas.
papers.abstract: This cross‑sectional observational study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to compare the microbiomes of periapical granulomas from primary and persistent apical periodontitis to identify microbial taxa and functional pathways associated with persistent lesions.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to compare the microbial communities within periapical granulomas from primary versus persistent apical periodontitis, aiming to identify taxa and functional pathways linked to lesion persistence. The findings highlight specific microbial signatures and metabolic functions that distinguish persistent lesions from primary ones, offering clues to why some infections resist treatment.

papers.title: A Two-Stage ESM-Based Machine Learning Pipeline for Robust Hierarchically Evaluated Enzyme Function Prediction.
papers.abstract: Accurate enzyme annotation remains a major bottleneck in translating rapidly growing protein sequence data into biological knowledge. Enzyme Commission (EC) prediction is particularly challenging because enzyme functions are organized hierarchically, annotations are often imbalanced across classes, and sequence similarity alone may be insufficient to resolve functional differences. To address these challenges, we developed ESM-ECForest, a 2-stage framework that combines protein embeddings generated by the pretrained language model ESM-2 (Evolutionary Scale Modeling 2) with random forest classi
papers.summary: The authors present ESM-ECForest, a two-stage machine learning pipeline that uses protein language model embeddings (ESM-2) combined with random forest classifiers to predict Enzyme Commission (EC) numbers. The approach explicitly accounts for the hierarchical organization of enzyme function and class imbalance, aiming to improve robustness over sequence-similarity-based annotation. This offers a practical tool for enzyme functional annotation as sequence databases continue to grow.

papers.title: Microbiota-mediated blocking of plasmodium falciparum sporozoites in Anopheles: a systematic review.
papers.abstract: The development of Plasmodium falciparum sporozoites in the mosquito, Anopheles, is essential for malaria transmission. Despite the unsurprising fact that the mosquito microbiota has become a major factor in the modulation of the competence of mosquitoes, the specific types of microbial taxa and mechanisms affecting the development of the sporozoite are not well synthesized. This systematic review brings together and critically evaluates the available evidence to understand the role of microbiota in the development of P. falciparum sporozoites in Anopheles mosquitoes with a specific focus on t
papers.summary: This systematic review synthesizes evidence on how the mosquito microbiota influences the development of Plasmodium falciparum sporozoites in Anopheles mosquitoes, focusing on which microbial taxa and mechanisms block sporozoite development. It consolidates findings across studies to clarify the role of specific bacteria and their interactions with the parasite, highlighting gaps in mechanistic understanding. The review is useful for researchers exploring microbiota-based strategies to reduce malaria transmission.

papers.title: Changes in the Gut Microbiota Composition and Metabolic Pathways in Six-Week-Old HIV Exposed Breastfed Infants Receiving Antiretroviral Prophylaxis.
papers.abstract: Understanding the association of HIV exposure, antiretroviral therapy (ART) prophylaxis and human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs) on the gut microbiota of breastfed infants is crucial for developing strategies to promote infant health. Our study explored gut microbiota diversity and development in breastfed infants, analysing the influence of nevirapine (NVP) in HIV Exposed infants and HMOs in HIV Unexposed infants.
papers.summary: This study examined how HIV exposure and antiretroviral prophylaxis (nevirapine) affect gut microbiota composition and metabolic pathways in six-week-old breastfed infants, comparing HIV-exposed infants receiving prophylaxis with HIV-unexposed infants. The researchers also considered the influence of human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs) on microbiota development. The findings highlight differences in microbial diversity and metabolic function associated with HIV exposure and antiretroviral prophylaxis during early infancy.

papers.title: Edible insect-based feed ingredients as modulators of gastrointestinal physiology in monogastric livestock and aquaculture species.
papers.abstract: Edible insects have emerged as promising sustainable feed ingredients capable of supporting both animal production and gastrointestinal health. Beyond their nutritional value, insect-derived meals contain bioactive compounds-including chitin, antimicrobial peptides, medium-chain fatty acids, micronutrients, and antioxidant molecules-that may modulate gut microbiota-host interactions in farmed monogastric animal species. This review critically examines current evidence on the mechanisms through which insect-based diets influence gastrointestinal physiology in livestock and aquaculture species.
papers.summary: This review examines how edible insect-based feed ingredients can influence gastrointestinal physiology in monogastric livestock and aquaculture species. It highlights that beyond basic nutrition, insect meals contain bioactive compounds such as chitin, antimicrobial peptides, medium-chain fatty acids, and antioxidants that may modulate gut microbiota-host interactions. The authors critically assess current evidence for these mechanisms and their potential to support both animal production and gut health.

papers.title: Clear aligner interface properties, oral microbial ecology, and strategies for biofilm control and caries-risk mitigation: a scoping review.
papers.abstract: Clear aligners create an aligner-tooth interface that may retain saliva, microorganisms, and dietary substrates. Evidence linking interface properties, oral microecological responses, and preventive interventions remains fragmented.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This scoping review examines how the physical interface created by clear aligners may trap saliva, microbes, and food, potentially altering oral microbial ecology and increasing caries risk. It synthesizes fragmented evidence on interface properties, microbial shifts, and preventive strategies such as biofilm control to mitigate these risks.

papers.title: Characterization of lower-airway microbial communities in pulmonary tuberculosis by BALF metagenomic sequencing.
papers.abstract: Pulmonary tuberculosis (PTB) is an infectious disease caused by the Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex (MTBC). This study aimed to characterize the lower-airway microbiome in patients with PTB and compare it with that of patients without PTB (Non-PTB) undergoing bronchoscopy for pulmonary disease, in order to describe differences in microbial composition between the two groups and improve our understanding of pulmonary microbial ecology in tuberculosis.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study used metagenomic sequencing of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) to characterize the lower-airway microbial communities in patients with pulmonary tuberculosis compared to non-TB patients undergoing bronchoscopy. It describes differences in microbial composition between the two groups, aiming to improve understanding of pulmonary microbial ecology in tuberculosis. The work provides a descriptive baseline of the lower-airway microbiome in PTB.

papers.title: Decoding pyroptosis at single-cell resolution: heterogeneity, microenvironment remodeling and potential translational insights.
papers.abstract: Pyroptosis, a pro-inflammatory programmed cell death mediated by inflammatory caspases and Gasdermin (GSDM) family proteins, exerts dual roles in host defense and pathological damage. Traditional bulk RNA sequencing (bulk RNA-seq) is limited in capturing single-cell heterogeneity and dissecting intercellular communication, impeding in-depth mechanistic exploration of pyroptosis. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) has emerged as a powerful tool to address these limitations, enabling high-throughput profiling of single-cell transcriptomes and precise characterization of gene expression heter
papers.summary: This review discusses how single-cell RNA sequencing is being used to study pyroptosis, an inflammatory form of programmed cell death driven by caspases and Gasdermin proteins. The authors argue that scRNA-seq overcomes the limitations of bulk RNA-seq by revealing cell-to-cell heterogeneity in pyroptotic gene expression and by enabling analysis of how pyroptotic cells reshape their surrounding microenvironment. The paper also highlights potential translational implications of these single-cell insights.

papers.title: Harnessing metatranscriptomics to unveil the metabolic landscape of microbiota in traditional fermented foods.
papers.abstract: Traditional fermented foods are widely consumed and valued for their distinctive sensory properties and potential health benefits. These foods contain complex microbiota whose interactions and metabolic activities shape biochemical transformations relevant to product quality, safety, and functionality. Metatranscriptomics provides a culture-independent means of profiling community RNA and examining changes in microbial gene expression during fermentation. However, most fermented-food microbiome studies continue to infer function from community composition or genomic potential rather than from
papers.summary: This review argues that metatranscriptomics—sequencing community RNA rather than DNA—can reveal which microbial genes are actually active during traditional fermented food production, going beyond the functional inferences typically drawn from community composition or genomic potential. It surveys how this approach can map the metabolic landscape of fermenting microbiota and connect gene expression to product quality, safety, and functionality.

papers.title: Dietary exogenous microRNAs in the gut: biological effects, mechanistic evidence, and controversies.
papers.abstract: Dietary exogenous microRNAs (miRNAs) have emerged as potential mediators of interorganismal communication, with growing interest in their ability to influence gastrointestinal physiology and the gut microbiota. These molecules encompass plant-derived miRNAs implicated in cross-kingdom regulation, animal-derived dietary miRNAs involved in cross-species communication, and maternal milk miRNAs that may participate in mother-to-offspring molecular crosstalk. A proportion of dietary miRNAs are associated with extracellular vesicles or other protective complexes, which may enhance their stability du
papers.summary: This review examines dietary microRNAs from plants, animals, and milk that may survive digestion and influence gut physiology and microbiota through cross-kingdom or cross-species communication. It discusses the protective role of extracellular vesicles in stabilizing these molecules and weighs the evidence against ongoing controversies about whether dietary miRNAs have meaningful biological effects in the gut.

papers.title: Building biologically relevant in vitro models of the human gut microbiota: methodological considerations, current challenges, and future perspectives.
papers.abstract: The human gut microbiota (HGM) plays a pivotal role in human health by regulating metabolic, immune, and neurological processes and contributes to the susceptibility to various diseases. The increasing interest in microbiota-targeted therapies has highlighted the need for in vitro models capable of accurately reproducing the composition, function, and ecological dynamics of the intestinal microbial ecosystem. This review examines the methodological factors that determine the biological relevance of HGM in vitro models, emphasizing that reliable experimental outcomes depend not only on the choi
papers.summary: This review examines the methodological factors that determine how biologically relevant in vitro models of the human gut microbiota can be, arguing that reliable experimental outcomes depend on more than just the choice of model system. It surveys current challenges in reproducing the composition, function, and ecological dynamics of the intestinal microbial ecosystem and outlines future perspectives for improving these models.

papers.title: Interpretable detection-based image classification for differential diagnosis of vaginal discharge using smartphone-assisted microscopy.
papers.abstract: The vaginal discharge is a common clinical presentation associated with diverse infectious and microbiota-related conditions. Existing artificial intelligence (AI)-based diagnostic approaches have predominantly focused on detection of individual pathogens and have rarely integrated microbiota-associated conditions within a diagnostic framework. We developed an explainable deep learning framework for automated analysis of Gram-stained vaginal smear images acquired using handheld smartphones or tablets positioned over a conventional light microscope eyepiece.
papers.summary: The authors developed an explainable deep learning framework that analyzes Gram-stained vaginal smear images captured by smartphones or tablets held over a conventional microscope eyepiece. Unlike prior AI approaches that detect individual pathogens, this framework integrates microbiota-associated conditions into a differential diagnosis of vaginal discharge, aiming to make microscopy-based diagnosis more accessible and interpretable.
